item.title: Paladin watch parties are on campus, in Greenville and all across the country
item.description: For the second time in four years, Furman is playing in the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament and watch parties are scheduled for Friday across the country.

item.title: Furman superfans take their part in the basketball tournament as seriously as the team
item.description: The Hammer family are part of a community of fans around the world who cheer on the Paladins home and away.

item.title: FOX Carolina's Ella Grogan talks one-on-one with Furman Men's Basketball
item.description: Furman alumna Ella Grogan '25 is traveling with the Paladins for the NCAA Tournament. She talks one-on-one with players and Head Coach Bob Richey ahead of Friday's first-round showdown with UConn.

item.title: Francis Kim writes article about oil-related impacts on U.S. dollar
item.description: Furman Associate Professor of Finance Francis Kim is a regular contributor for Korea JoongAng Daily. He offers historical context for the U.S. dollar and rising oil prices following the U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran.

item.title: Courtney Tollison included in 'Celebrating South Carolina Women'
item.description: Furman's Courtney Tollison '99, Distinguished University Public Historian and Scholar, is recognized among 50 South Carolina women making an impact by the publishers of "Who's on the Move."

item.title: No. 2 Seed UConn Survives Against No. 15 Seed Furman In NCAA Tournament First Round, 82-71
item.description: No. 15 seed Furman Paladins men's basketball saw its run in the NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament come to a close with a first-round loss 82-71 to No. 2 seed UConn Huskies

item.title: Local news covers first-round play at NCAA Tournament, Paladins vs. Huskies
item.description: Furman players and Head Coach Bob Richey reflect on the Paladins' loss to No. 2 seed UConn at the NCAA Tournament. "They didn't go down without a fight," writes one reporter. Another reporter notes the matchup was one of the most fascinating schematic games of the tournament.

item.title: Mentorship in Action at Furman Engaged
item.description: Shaniece Criss and Roger Abim-Karmon are just two examples of the mentorship that happens throughout a Furman student’s academic career leading up to Furman Engaged.

item.title: Brendan Talwar '11 talks 'All the Sharks' on WSPA's 'Your Carolina'
item.description: Brendan Talwar '11 and his research partner talk "All the Sharks" and more in a conversation aired on WSPA's "Your Carolina." Talwar says his passion for conservation began at Furman.

item.title: Undergraduate student presents at national chemistry symposium
item.description: Undergraduate research is part of Furman’s DNA, and senior Skylar Delozier won an opportunity to present her years of research at a national conference.

item.title: Sierra Burns M’29 made headlines at February’s State of the Union for her advocacy of the foster care system
item.description: As Sierra Burns earns her master’s degree at Furman, she’s also working full time at Prisma, advocating for a foster care bill at the South Carolina statehouse and being invited to the State of the Union.

item.title: Furman Engaged was a steppingstone for Fretwell ’16
item.description: From an internship at a local crisis shelter to presenting his experiences to crowds, Joe Fretwell applies what he learned at Furman every day in his career.

item.title: Erin Wamsley quoted in TIME about memory and learning
item.description: A TIME magazine story about memory and learning quotes Furman's Wamsley, who pushes back on the idea that rest is a waste of time. Rather, "offline states" are necessary for memory consolidation.

item.title: Liz Seman named to South Carolina's Top 100 Women
item.description: Liz Seman, Furman chief of staff and VP for community and government relations, earns a place on South Carolina's list of Top 100 Women.

item.title: Brent Nelsen comments on GOP debate for SC governor's race
item.description: Furman's Brent Nelsen says candidates' participation in the GOP debates hinges on individual campaign strategies.
